facts.value: Nurses are at risk for workplace violence and abuse.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Three types of workplace violence: physical violence (hitting, kicking, beating, punching, biting, and using objects); psychological violence (threats or coercion); sexual violence (attempted/completed non-consensual sex act).
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Interpersonal violence is committed by workers or patients and their families, primarily manifesting as verbal abuse.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Organizational coercion may include excessive workloads, mandatory shifts, involuntary placement in another part of the workplace, low salaries, denial of benefits/overtime, and poor working environment.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Factors can be divided into environmental, organizational, and individual psychosocial factors.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Environmental factors include the specific setting, long patient wait times, frequent interruptions, uncertainty regarding patients' treatment, and heavy workloads.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Organizational factors include inefficient teamwork, organizational injustice, lack of aggression- and stress-management programs, and distrust between colleagues.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Individual psychosocial factors may include young and inexperienced nurses, previous experiences with violence, and lack of communication skills.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Misunderstandings may occur due to the communication barrier between nurses and patients.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: 80% of serious violent incidents in health care centers were committed by patients.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Workplace violence has negative emotional and physical impacts on nurses, causing feelings of depersonalization, dehumanization, exhaustion, and stress.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online

facts.value: Nurses have reported burn-out due to frequent exposure to workplace violence.
facts.programme_association: Nursing Education Master’s Concentration – MSN | ASU Online
